picks.style: doric victory ode, kithara and low drone, layered male chorus, stately, awed, spacious
picks.why: 'One race of men, one race of gods' — and man is nothing, while the bronze sky stands forever. Pindar's most quoted lines.

picks.style: greek heroic lament, lyre and frame drum, grieving tenor answered by a low voice, slow, tender, dialogic
picks.why: Polydeuces weeping over the dying Castor and asking Zeus to let him die too — a complete scene with a god's reply.

picks.style: gnomic ode, plucked lyre and soft aulos, wry knowing male voice, measured, sardonic, level
picks.why: Homer's lies given their solemnity, Ajax undone by a vote, and rich and poor travelling together to the boundary of death.

picks.style: late antique pastoral lament, solo reed pipe and soft harp, dying tenor, very slow, tender, fading
picks.why: The dying shepherd asking for anemones over his grave and one tear, enough to wet her cheek — flawless and self-contained.

picks.style: greek elegiac aria, lyre and low strings, raw grieving voice, slow, imploring, broken
picks.why: Dionysus begging Zeus for one hour of Ampelos's speech — 'I have eyes, and I do not see you grieving'.

picks.style: dionysiac hymn, double aulos, hand drums and cymbals, ecstatic massed voices, driving, whirling, ecstatic
picks.why: The prophecy of wine: the reddening vine, the treaders at the press, the Bassarids shaking their hair and shouting Euoi.

picks.style: english elegiac air, cello and harpsichord, grave tenor, slow, brooding, unresolved
picks.why: 'Where shall affliction from itself retire?' — care blotting the sun, sighing in the grove, murmuring in the stream.

picks.style: rural ballad, fiddle and low guitar, weathered male voice, slow, plain, unsparing
picks.why: The old ploughman who once made the straightest furrow, now disdained by the rich and by the poor alike.

picks.style: english hymn-tune, chamber organ and viola, plain steady voice, moderate, reflective, settled
picks.why: 'When all the fiercer passions cease' — proper quatrains, and the whole of late wisdom in eight lines.

picks.style: english ballad, guitar and flute, small clear female voice, gentle, pleading, strophic
picks.why: The mouse's petition from the trap — 'never let thine heart be shut against the prisoner's cries' — her best-known poem.

picks.style: dissenting hymn, unaccompanied voices with soft organ, warm alto, slow, resolute, building
picks.why: Every crop and flock and rain taken away, and the last line still 'love thee — for thyself alone'.

picks.style: night meditation, sustained strings and soft bells, hushed contralto, very slow, spacious, luminous
picks.why: 'How deep the silence, yet how loud the praise!' and a tongue in every star — the midnight as the noon of thought.

picks.style: gothic ode, low strings and distant horn, dark contralto, slow, airless, oppressive
picks.why: Melancholy's country where gales forget to blow and currents cease to flow, and Care lies down on Grief's lap.

picks.style: dramatic ode, tremolo strings and hissing percussion, urgent male voice, taut, sinister, building
picks.why: Envy's cell under the barren rocks — 'at Merit's name prepar'd to shed their influence all her snaky tresses hiss'.

picks.style: english devotional ode, chamber organ and strings, declamatory tenor, measured, mounting, questioning
picks.why: The owl shutting its eyes against the day, then the sky and the flowers each summoned to answer who made them.

picks.style: vedantic chant, tanpura drone and small cymbals, deep male voice, very slow, austere, sparse
picks.why: No fear even of death from death itself, and the reed and plantain that perish once they have flowered.

picks.style: sanskrit devotional recitation, drone and soft bell, calm low voice, slow, unfolding, still
picks.why: Release with no place to go to — only the knot of ignorance split — and the lotus-leaf untouched by the water.

picks.style: greek sea-hymn, lyre and hand drum, clear ringing male voice, rolling, buoyant, ceremonial
picks.why: Only candidate, but it carries Arion's whole hymn to Poseidon — the dolphins dancing in a ring and carrying him ashore.

picks.style: english gnomic air, lute and hand drum, bold plain voice, brisk, epigrammatic, spurring
picks.why: Only candidate: three epigraphs that happen to agree — audacious ignorance beats timid knowledge, so spur boldly on.
